overall_summary: A black bear enters a rural backyard and investigates one classic oscillating lawn sprinkler. The sprinkler is visibly connected by one hose to the house spigot and sprays several readable water arcs. Grandma first appears inside the visible house doorway, then walks along the unobstructed path and reacts while the bear gets startled and leaves by the same open route.
tone: Unplanned real-life backyard security-camera footage: ordinary, observational, imperfect, funny because the event is unexpectedly real, never cinematic, staged, polished, promotional, or commercial.
capture_style: One fixed elevated outdoor security-camera viewpoint with mild fisheye distortion, natural daylight, ordinary exposure, and no camera operator movement.
visual_style: Real rural backyard beside a modest light-colored house. Keep the house wall and one visible back door on the left, one open grass route on the right, one garden path from the door, one green hose, and one old-fashioned metal oscillating lawn sprinkler in the foreground-center.
visual_realism: The spigot, single hose, sprinkler, water outlet, bear, doorway, path, and grass must form one continuous physical layout. The hose must visibly connect the house spigot to the sprinkler base, and every water stream must visibly originate at the sprinkler head.
audio_policy: Natural location sound only: sprinkler clicks and water spray, grass movement, bear footsteps, Grandma's distant natural voice, and outdoor birds.
camera_lock: Keep one completely fixed elevated security-camera viewpoint for the entire shot. No pan, tilt, zoom, cut, alternate angle, camera push-in, or changing architecture.
continuity_invariants: Exactly one bear, one Grandma, one house, one door, one spigot, one green hose, and one metal oscillating sprinkler remain throughout.
The hose stays connected from the house spigot to the sprinkler base; it never becomes a second hose or changes endpoint.
The sprinkler stays planted in the foreground-center and emits several separate, visible arcs from its sprinkler head; water never shoots from bare ground or the bear's mouth.
The bear's route is open grass at the right edge to the sprinkler, then back out along the same open grass route.
Grandma's route is the visible house doorway to the unobstructed garden path; she never enters through a wall, railing, or hidden corner.

panel_convention: Eight chronological landscape panels in a clean 2-by-4 storyboard sheet with thin black borders. Each panel has a white caption band beneath the image with its frame number and exact caption. Keep all text in the caption bands and never inside the image areas.
hard_constraints: Show the bear's entry route before it reaches the sprinkler.
Show Grandma at the actual doorway before she walks onto the path.
Show exactly one hose connected to the spigot and visibly terminating at the sprinkler base.
Show every water stream originating from the sprinkler head; no water may appear to come from bare ground, the hose tip, or the bear's mouth.
Use one classic metal oscillating sprinkler with several readable arcs, not a hidden nozzle or magical fountain.
Do not show the bear spitting water; the final reaction is a physical shake of wet fur.
Do not duplicate or morph the bear, Grandma, house, doorway, hose, sprinkler, or path.
Preserve one fixed camera and identical yard geometry in every panel.
